title: canary release scratchpad - jordan lee
content:
Goal: validate runtime + model variant (gptx-2.1 quantized) under production traffic shape for latency, throughput, and quality. Quick notes and checklist for the staged canary we want to run this week.

Context:
- Target: hosted API route /v1/generate (prod cluster us-west-2).
- Model: redwood/gptx-2.1-quantized-v3 (primary canary).
- Fallback model for safety: redwood/gptx-2.0-stable.
- Reason: new kernel selection + KV cache change in runtime PR #1129. Need to ensure no perf or quality regressions.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Are autoscaling policies for canary pods identical to prod? I think yes but verify memory headroom when quantized variant has larger host mem.
- Does metric sampler capture tail-latency properly for small 1% traffic? (we may need synthetic spike tests)

Quick checklist (order-of-ops):
1) Preflight (at least 24h before):
   - [ ] Confirm PR 1129 merged to release branch and image built (tag: runtime-release-2026-02-27).
   - [ ] Build canary model bundle and upload to model registry: tag redwood/gptx-2.1-qv3-canary-20260227.
   - [ ] Pin canary route config in routing service (route: route-canary-gptx-2.1).
   - [ ] Add canary to rollout config in Console (canary id: canary-2026-02-jlee).
   - [ ] Create Grafana dashboard snapshot for baseline (link copied to linked_artifacts).
   - [ ] Create Eval set: 200 prompts from production prompt-bank (eval set id: canary-quickset-20260227).

2) Smoke (0% -> 1%):
   - [ ] Deploy canary with 0% traffic but warm caches (preload KV cached prefixes using synthetic warmup job).
   - [ ] Run smoke traffic: 1000 synthetic requests at small concurrency; verify no immediate OOMs, no increased error rates.
   - [ ] Check logs for exceptions related to kernel selection / quantization paths.

3) Ramp (1% -> 10% over ~2h):
   - Ramp plan: 1% -> 2% -> 5% -> 10% (30m -> 30m -> 60m).
   - Monitoring to watch continuously:
     * error_rate (5m) > 0.5% -> notify on-call + pause ramp
     * error_rate (5m) > 1.0% for 5m -> rollback to previous pinned model
     * p95 latency increase > 30% vs baseline for 10m -> pause and investigate
     * quality eval: %pass on canary-quickset drop > 3% absolute -> rollback
     * CPU/GPU utilization anomalies (unexpected host CPU or memory spikes) -> pause
   - [ ] During each step: grab sample outputs (50 examples) and compare against baseline using automatic diff script (scripts/canary/diff_outputs.sh).

4) Steady state (10% for 24h):
   - [ ] Run full eval (200 prompts) every 2 hours and push results to /canary-results.
   - [ ] Monitor customer-facing metrics (latency, SLA violations) and internal logs.
   - [ ] Run adversarial prompt set overnight (20k requests) to exercise long-tail behaviour.

5) Post-canary decision:
   - [ ] If everything OK: schedule canary -> gradually increase to 50% next week and coordinate with infra for capacity.
   - [ ] If any failure: immediate rollback and postmortem. Assign owner for RCA.

Rollback criteria (formalized):
- Any of the following triggers an automatic rollback to the previous pinned model variant:
  * 5m sustained error_rate > 1.0%
  * p95 latency > baseline p95 * 1.5 for >= 10 minutes
  * Eval-set pass rate drops by >= 3 percentage points vs baseline across 3 consecutive eval runs
  * Observed OOMs or repeated kernel selection errors in logs

Version pinning notes:
- Production pinned model currently: redwood/gptx-2.0-stable@sha256:abcd1234 (config: default-kernel, float16).
- For canary we will pin routing rule to redwood/gptx-2.1-qv3-canary-20260227@sha256:efgh5678.
- Must ensure rollout policy includes automatic fallback mapping in routing table so traffic can revert without needing control-plane write.
- Record model bundle checksum in canary metadata doc and in release PR.

Operational runbook snippets (to paste into on-call notes):
- To pause ramp: POST /api/rollouts/{canary-id}/pause (curl provided in release PR).
- To rollback: POST /api/rollouts/{canary-id}/rollback -> that triggers route mapping to previous model.
- To collect logs: use loki query: {job="runtime-canary", canary_id="canary-2026-02-jlee"} |= "ERROR" |~ "kernel|OOM|exception"

Short TODOs for me:
- [ ] Confirm warmup job includes both kv-prefix and attention-cache primes for seq-len=1024.
- [ ] Add a quickstep in Console to show model checksum next to model name (ask DevExp).
- [ ] Draft post-canary email template for PMs/CS with perf/quality summary.

Notes from last run (2025-11 canary):
- Observed small increase in tail-latency attributed to suboptimal kernel fallback on certain matmul shapes; fixed by PR 987 which added better kernel heuristics.
- Need better sampling for quality regression detection (current random sample missed subtle hallucination case).

Unresolved/risks:
- If quantized variant interacts poorly with new memory allocator, could cause host-side OOMs under warmup. We should keep node replacement strategy ready.
- Need a longer eval set for dialog flows (current eval is mostly single-turn).

Relevant commands / snippets:
- Warmup job (k8s): kubectl apply -f k8s/warmup-job-canary.yaml --namespace=prod-canary
- Diff outputs: ./scripts/canary/diff_outputs.sh redwood/gptx-2.0-stable redwood/gptx-2.1-qv3-canary-20260227 sample-50.json
- Pause rollout: curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://console.api.redwood.ai/rollouts/canary-2026-02-jlee/pause"

If anything goes sideways ping Aisha and Miguel immediately (Slack: #oncall-release).

-- jordan
